_why: One name per idea, for the half of the API that is behaviour. lint:vocab holds the shared props to one set of VALUES and lint:api holds every prop name to one TYPE; neither stops a part inventing a twenty-third word for a thing the system already names. On 2026-09-02 this catalogue published 32 callback names for about eight ideas, and writing one specimen against them means guessing.
_decided: 2026-09-03. The first version of this file called every name outside the six an exception waiting to be renamed, and applying that table would have made several APIs WORSE: `onBack` is not one action among many, `onExpandedChange` says which value moved and `onChange` does not, `onClear` on a search field does not fire on typing so calling it a change would be a lie. So the file now decides rather than defers. `canonical` is the vocabulary a new part must speak. `kept` is a name that stays, each with the thing it says that the canonical one cannot — a decision, not debt. `exceptions` is what is still wrong and what it will become.

canonical.onChange: The value this part owns became a different value. The argument is the new value, never an event.
canonical.onSelect: One of several offered things was chosen. The argument names what was chosen.
canonical.onOpenChange: A layer this part owns opened or closed. The argument is the new open state, so one name covers both directions and a controlled caller needs no second prop.
canonical.onDismiss: The person asked to be rid of it — Escape, the backdrop, the close control. Distinct from onOpenChange because a dismissal is a request that a caller may refuse.
canonical.onSubmit: A form was sent. The argument is what was collected.
canonical.onAction: A named action on this part was invoked. The argument says which one, so a part with five actions does not publish five callbacks.

kept._why: Each of these says something the six cannot, and the reason is the entry. A name here is a decision that has been argued; adding one is the same work.
kept.onClose: The layers that publish it render only while they are open, so there is no open STATE to report — `onOpenChange(false)` would be the only call it ever makes. It is a dismissal request under an older name, and renaming it to onDismiss would touch 263 call sites in eight products to change nothing a reader can see. Reopened when a layer needs to report both directions.
kept.onBack: Not one action among several: it is the way out of a screen, it sits in a named slot, and it comes with `backLabel` beside it. `onAction` would say less and disagree with its own label.
kept.onCancel: The control it belongs to is labelled Cancel by `cancelLabel`. A callback whose name disagrees with the words on its own button is worse than a name outside the six.
kept.onClear: It does NOT fire when the value changes — a search field clearing is one specific act, and the field itself reports typing through the input it spreads onto. Calling it onChange would promise a call that never comes.
kept.onExpandedChange: Says WHICH value moved, on a part whose selection is a different callback. `onChange` on a tree would leave a reader guessing between the two.
kept.onCollapsedChange: The same, for a rail that also reports selection.
kept.onDensityChange: A second value on a table toolbar that already reports its filters, and the pair is legible only while both say what they carry.
kept.onSortChange: The same, for a grid that also reports cell edits.
kept.onCellChange: The other half of that pair.
kept.onMonthChange: A calendar publishes onChange for the DATE. The month is what is on screen, not what was chosen, and one word cannot be both.
kept.onNavOpen: One half of a shell that moves its own rail; the pair is the mechanism and `onOpenChange` would be a third state nobody sets.
kept.onDetailClose: A page whose detail panel closes while the page stays. `onDismiss` belongs to the thing being dismissed, and here the page is not it.
kept.onLoad: One job, named for it. `onAction` on a part with a single action is a name that has to be looked up.
kept.onSave: The same, and it pairs with a control the reader sees labelled Save.
kept.onSend: The same, in a composer where sending is the point.
kept.onStop: The other end of that composer: what stops a run in flight, which is not an action among many but the one that interrupts.
kept.onAbort: The same idea one part over, and both stay until the two are one mechanism.
kept.onReset: Back to the defaults, which is not a value change: the caller decides what the defaults are.
kept.onMove: A column changed places. The argument is a direction, which onAction would flatten.
kept.onRemove: Taking one thing out of many, where onAction would need an argument to say which and there already is one.
kept.onDislike: A specific judgement about a message, and the only one this part reports.
kept.onNext: Advances a stack that has no other action.
kept.onClick: One part publishes it, and it is the DOM name for a pill whose whole body is one button. It stays until that pill is either a Button or an action list.

exceptions._why: Still wrong, and what each becomes. config/api-debt.json freezes which parts carry them so an exception cannot spread while it waits.

onOpen.why: a card that opens is a card the reader CHOSE; there is no open state to report and the three parts that publish it navigate rather than reveal
